_comment: Canonical label taxonomy for the leaf disease model. 'canonical_labels' is the exact 38-class vocabulary extracted from the currently deployed MLModel1.mlnet - do not rename these or the existing model's classes will no longer line up with a fine-tuned successor. Add new canonical labels at the bottom of the list when you bring in a crop/disease that isn't covered yet.

sources.name: plantvillage_official
sources._comment: Official PlantVillage release (huggingface.co/datasets/mohanty/PlantVillage), CC BY-SA 3.0. Same underlying data the original Kaggle 'New Plant Diseases Dataset' was augmented from, but with a leak-safe 80/20 split (grouped by physical leaf) instead of a naive random split. Folder names already match canonical_labels exactly, so no mapping is needed. Organized into train/valid folders by scripts/organize_plantvillage.py from data.zip + the official split lists.

sources.name: plantwild
sources._comment: PlantWild v2 (huggingface.co/datasets/uqtwei2/PlantWild), CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Real-world/in-the-wild photos, 115 disease classes, zero healthy classes. Only 22 of its 115 classes correspond to something in canonical_labels - the rest (new crops like rice/wheat/coffee/banana, and a few diseases this taxonomy doesn't cover) are intentionally left unmapped per the decision to keep the model scoped to the existing 38 classes; they'll land in _unmapped/ on merge.

sources.name: EXAMPLE_new_source
sources._comment: Template for a new dataset. Run `python prepare_dataset.py discover --source <path>` first to list its actual leaf folder names, then fill in 'mapping' below: source folder name -> canonical label. Map to a brand-new label (not in canonical_labels above) to introduce a new class - add it to canonical_labels too. Any source folder you don't map is copied into <out>/_unmapped/<name>/ instead of being silently dropped or guessed.
